nodes.label: CritPt: Complex Research using Integrated Thinking - Physics Test
nodes.author: Minhui Zhu, Minyang Tian, et al.
nodes.rationale: Benchmark of 71 unpublished research-level physics challenges (190 checkpoints) covering 11 disciplines; designed to probe LLM reasoning at frontier research level with guess-resistant, machine-verifiable answers and physics-informed auto-grading pipeline.

nodes.label: Challenge-Checkpoint Decomposition
nodes.rationale: Each full challenge decomposed into 2-4 checkpoints isolating specific reasoning steps; preserves depth of realistic research workflow while enabling fine-grained analysis of failure modes and identification of modular tasks LLMs can assist with today.

nodes.label: Two-Step Answer Generation Protocol
nodes.rationale: Step 1: free-form solution reasoning without formatting constraints; Step 2: standardized answer extraction into code block template; disentangles reasoning from formatting to avoid premature conversions and reduce parsing errors from inconsistent model output styles.

nodes.label: Physics-Informed Auto-Grading System
nodes.rationale: Supports three answer types (numerical, symbolic, Python functions) with expert-provided tolerances and custom SymPy routines; enables scalable, high-fidelity evaluation of diverse complex output formats in advanced physics with sandboxed execution and resource limits.

nodes.label: Consistently Solved Rate Reliability Metric
nodes.rationale: Problem deemed consistently solved if ≥4 of 5 independent runs yield correct answer; stricter than average accuracy to probe reliability and trustworthiness; reveals high stochasticity in LLM behavior on complex physics problems.

nodes.label: GPT-5 Performance on CritPt
nodes.rationale: Best base model achieves 5.7% average accuracy on 70 challenges; improves to 10.6% with code interpreter and 12.6% with code+web search; only 4.3% consistently solved rate, indicating fundamental reasoning bottlenecks despite tool access.

nodes.label: Frontier Physics Research Reasoning
nodes.rationale: Reasoning demands of modern physics research: mathematical rigor, true creativity, precise execution, consistency between theory and experiment; characterized by broad scopes, open-ended questions, deep decision trees, sparse solution spaces; fundamentally different from textbook problems.
